pid_data.process_description: Process Overview The highlighted section of the P&ID represents the VCM charging and transfer system that primarily delivers Vinyl Chloride Monomer (VCM) from the fresh VCM storage tanks SV-101A/B to the polymerization reactor SR-301 through the red-line flow path. In addition to the fresh VCM supply, the system also interfaces with the recovered VCM storage tanks SV-111A/B, which serve as an alternate or recovery source within the overall VCM handling system; however, SV-111A/B and their associated routing are not part of the red-line highlighted transfer path. The active charging path includes SV-101A/B, transfer pumps SP-101A/B, filters SF-101A/B and SF-107A/B, and the associated piping, valves, and instrumentation required to ensure controlled and safe VCM charging into the reactor. Process Initiation Under normal operation, the process begins with liquid VCM stored in the fresh VCM tanks SV-101A/B. When charging is required, the tank outlet isolation valves are opened and one of the transfer pumps SP-101A/B is started. VCM is withdrawn from the selected storage tank and enters the red-line piping system, where initial filtration and instrumentation verify that pressure, flow, and temperature conditions are suitable for downstream transfer. The recovered VCM tanks SV-111A/B remain isolated during normal red-line operation and are maintained as standby or recovery inventory. If operations require the use of recovered VCM, SV-111A/B can be aligned through dedicated connections outside the red-line charging route. Process End The process concludes when the required quantity of VCM is delivered into reactor SR-301 through the designated feed connection. After completion of the charging operation, the transfer pumps are stopped and the relevant isolation valves are closed to secure the system and prevent unintended VCM movement prior to the reaction phase. Process Description Liquid VCM drawn from SV-101A/B is pressurized by transfer pumps SP-101A/B and conveyed through the red-line piping network. Along this route, the flow passes through filters SF-101A/B and SF-107A/B to remove particulates and ensure feed quality, followed by isolation valves for operational control, check valves to prevent reverse flow, and instrumented sections for continuous monitoring of pressure, flow, and temperature. The conditioned VCM stream then proceeds through the charging line toward the reactor feed header under controlled operating conditions until it enters SR-301. The recovered VCM tanks SV-111A/B are part of the broader VCM handling system for inventory management and recovery service, but their normal routing is hydraulically separated from the red-line charging path and therefore outside the active hazard scope of this specific P&ID segment. File Description The P&ID file (Red-Line and Red-circle Detection Scope) documents the piping and instrumentation configuration for the fresh VCM charging operation. For detection and analysis purposes, only the red-line and red-circle highlighted flow path is considered, covering SV-101A/B, SP-101A/B, SF-101A/B, SF-107A/B, associated piping, valves, instrumentation, and the reactor feed interface to SR-301. Recovered VCM systems, including SV-111A/B, as well as non-highlighted utilities, are outside the scope of the red-line detection, but are acknowledged as part of the overall VCM storage and recovery system.
